nodes.name: Receive quota request
nodes.notes: GET /webhook/join-quota. Deliberately public and without a secret: the answer is two numbers, how many of the daily requests are spent and how many there are. A secret would have to ship inside the delivered landing-page code, so anyone reading the page source would hold it - it would hide nothing and only add a way for the page to break. Allowed Origins (CORS) carries the same list as the status workflow; without it the browser discards the answer although the call itself succeeded.

nodes.name: Read counter
nodes.notes: Reads /home/node/.n8n/join-quota-state.json, the same file the issue collector writes. Missing file or a state from an earlier UTC day both answer used=0. Read-only - calling this endpoint never spends a quota slot. The limit of 10 sits here and in the guard of the issue collector and has to be changed in both.

nodes.name: Respond: counter
nodes.notes: Answers {"used": n, "limit": 10}. The landing page falls back to used=0 when this endpoint does not answer, so a dead n8n leaves the page usable instead of showing a limit that was never reached.
